correctness.rationale: Exact Kirchhoff heat kernel from Neumann/Dirichlet ray splitting; Gaussian row/column derivative integrals yield the norm formula for every positive time. A 71-assertion standalone checker corroborates finite identities, but none of the infinite claims depend on it.

originality.rationale: The known Kirchhoff heat kernel is explicitly credited to Kostrykin–Potthoff–Schrader. The new result is the strict ordering of optimized time-derivative endpoint norms across all integer ray counts and the positive, exactly characterized first-order 1/m loss to the infinite-ray Gaussian variational limit. Inspected original metric-tree heat estimates and close mathematical-record summaries do not state an optimized norm theorem that covers these assertions. The comparison is evidence for originality, not a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The normalized sharp endpoint analytic-semigroup derivative constant quantifies worst-case instantaneous heat-flow amplification on a natural metric star. Strict sensitivity to vertex degree, a nontrivial universal infinite-degree limit and a positive sharp reciprocal-degree correction reveal a structural branching mechanism missing from ordinary Gaussian kernel and trace estimates. The precise global invariant and correction are intrinsically motivated rather than arbitrary finite samples.
